questions_and_answers.question: Which phrase is identified as an unreal or subjunctive phrase expressing a polite request or suggestion?
According to the notes, what does adding 'gern' to an unreal phrase with a past participle often indicate?

answers.answer: It functions as a politeness formula or expresses a less urgent desire
It turns the phrase into a command

questions_and_answers.question: Which phrase is more commonly used to refer to past possibility?
In the sentence 'Wir hätten uns auch gern die Tannhäuser-Aufführung angehört, konnten aber keine Karten mehr bekommen', what does 'hätten gern' convey?
Which phrase can refer to both present and past possibility?
What does the example 'Ich wäre gern um zwölf Uhr nach Hause gegangen, aber jetzt ist es schon halb zwei' express?

answers.answer: The speaker would have liked to go home at twelve but it's now too late
The speaker is glad they went home early
The speaker is asking permission to leave
The speaker is planning to go at twelve

questions_and_answers.question: According to the notes, using 'wäre gern + past participle' with present reference has what effect?

answers.answer: It increases the degree of doubt about fulfilling the desire

questions_and_answers.question: What do the phrases 'hätte gern' and 'wäre gern' share with phrases referring to past possibility?

answers.answer: They use a different future auxiliary

questions_and_answers.question: Which section of Unit 20 deals with the phrases 'hätte gern' and 'wäre gern'?
When did the phrase 'hätte gern' previously appear as an unreal phrase according to the notes?

articles.text:
B.
VERBS.
THE UNREAL OR SUBJUNCTIVE PHRASES hätte gern + Past Participle
and wäre gern
+ Past Participle
I.
The phrase hätte gern was identified in Unit 18 as an UNREAL or SUBJUNCTlVE
phrase expressing a polite request or suggestion:
Ich hätte gern einen leichten
Anzug.
Ich hätte gern Rumpsteak mit
Röstkartoffeln.
I'm interested in a light-weight suit.
I'd like steak with fried potatoes.
It has occurred in the present unit with a past Participle:
Ich hätte mir gern noch ein
paar belegte Brötchen am
Buffet geholt.
I'd like to get a couple of sandwiches
from the refreshment bar before we go in.
You will notice that this phrase has the same form as the phrases discussed
in Unit 19 referring to PAST POSSIBILITY.
However, in this combination with
gern the meaning of the reference may actually be PRESENT POSSIBILITY.
The
use of the UNREAL or SUBJUNCTIVE phrase with the past participle is here a
politeness formula, expressing a less urgent desire or one more doubtful of
fulfillment.
II. More common is the use of the phrase hätte gern + Past Participle with
reference to PAST POSSIBILITY.
Here are some further examples:
Wir hätten uns auch gern die
Tannhäuser-Aufführung ange-
hört, konnten aber keine Kar-
ten mehr bekommen.
Sie hätten das Haus gern vor
dem Ende des Sommers verkauft.
We would have liked to go to the
'Tannhäuser' performance too, but
couldn't get tickets any more.
They would have liked to sell the
house before the end of the summer
('they wish they had sold ...').
III. The phrase with the auxiliary wäre + gern and Past Participle also occurs.
Note that it too may refer both to PRESENT and to PAST POSSIBILITY:
Ich wäre gern um zwölf Uhr
nach Hause gegangen, aber
jetzt ist es schon halb zwei.
Ich wäre gern um zwölf Uhr
nach Hause gegangen, aber
es sieht nicht so aus, als
ob das möglich sein wird.
I would have liked to go home ('wish
I had gone home') at twelve o'clock,
but now it's already one thirty.
I would like to go home ('I wish I could
go home') at twelve o'clock, but it doesn't
look as if that will be possible.
Here, too, in referring to PRESENT POSSIBILITY the use of this phrase with
the past participle serves to increase the degree of doubt expressed as to
whether the desire will be fulfilled.
